Religious Against Human Trafficking — Kenya

Where shattered lives find hope, and resilience blossoms into freedom

Since 2016, a network of consecrated religious, lay women and men has worked across Kenya to prevent human trafficking, protect survivors and restore dignity — through prayer, protection, prevention and partnership.

Support the work Who we are
Need help, or worried about someone? Call the toll-free helpline 0800 724 690 — free, confidential, from any network.
Since the Jubilee Year of Mercy

Talitha Kum International — Kenya

In 2016, TIK-RAHT began in Kenya during the Jubilee Year of Mercy, initiated by a collective effort of consecrated religious, lay women and men. Inspired by Pope Francis’ call to embody the corporal works of mercy, the organisation reaches out to those who live on the margins of society.

“Human trafficking is a crime against humanity. We must unite our efforts to free victims and stop this crime that’s become ever more aggressive, that threatens not just individuals, but the foundational values of society.” — Pope Francis
How we work

The four Ps that define us

PRAYER

Rooted in faith, we commit to uplifting both survivors and perpetrators through prayer, seeking transformation and fullness of life for all.

Explore

PROTECTION

We offer comprehensive care, from psychosocial support to medical aid and shelter, aimed at the holistic well-being of survivors.

Explore

PREVENTION

Through community workshops, training and media advocacy, we equip individuals and institutions to be first responders against human trafficking.

Explore

PARTNERSHIPS

Collaborating with a diverse network of stakeholders, we amplify our impact and stay abreast of trends in the fight against trafficking.

About us

A network of mercy, working to end trafficking in Kenya

Talitha Kum International Kenya — Religious Against Human Trafficking — has walked with survivors and communities since 2016.

How we began

Born in the Jubilee Year of Mercy

In 2016, TIK-RAHT began in Kenya during the Jubilee Year of Mercy. It was initiated by a collective effort of consecrated religious, lay women and men. Inspired by Pope Francis’ call to embody acts of mercy, particularly the corporal works of mercy, the organisation focuses on reaching out to and assisting those who reside on the margins of society.

The name comes from the Aramaic words spoken in the Gospel of Mark — “Talitha kum”: little girl, arise — and that is the work: helping those whom trafficking has knocked down to stand again.

“Human trafficking is a crime against humanity. We must unite our efforts to free victims and stop this crime.” — Pope Francis
How we work

The four Ps that define us

PRAYER

Rooted in faith, we commit to uplifting both survivors and perpetrators through prayer, seeking transformation and fullness of life for all.

Explore

PROTECTION

We offer comprehensive care, from psychosocial support to medical aid and shelter, aimed at the holistic well-being of survivors.

Explore

PREVENTION

Through community workshops, training and media advocacy, we equip individuals and institutions to be first responders and advocates against human trafficking.

Explore

PARTNERSHIPS

Collaborating with a diverse network of stakeholders, we amplify our impact and stay abreast of current trends in the fight against human trafficking.

Vision, Mission & Values

What guides everything we do

Three commitments, held by every congregation and partner in the network.

Our Vision

Inspired by the mercy of God, we envision a world free from human trafficking.

Our Mission

To uphold human dignity at all costs — from modern-day slavery to freedom — collaborating to eradicate human trafficking.

Our Values

Unity in Diversity Mutual Support Integrity Honesty Confidentiality Prayer

Walk with us

Every value on this page is lived out by people — in shelters, parishes, schools and border towns across Kenya. Join them.
